title: POC scoping: workload modeling for ElevatePay
next_steps: Redwood to share draft benchmark plan and test scripts (Priya)
ElevatePay to provide representative traffic traces and sample documents (Marcus)
Schedule 1-hour production-like benchmark window week of Jan 4th (tentative)
Send security/compliance docs and SOC2 summary (Alex)
action_items: Priya Shah (SE) - produce benchmark plan + containerized test harness - due 2027-01-04
Marcus Lee (CTO) - share 2 weeks of anonymized traffic traces + spike windows - due 2026-12-31
Daniel Park (SRE) - provide VPC network test account and firewall rules - due 2027-01-03
Alex Nguyen (AE) - send pricing band for Dedicated and Hosted pilot - due 2026-12-30
summary: Discovery / POC scoping to characterize ElevatePay workload for a 4-week pilot. Primary goals: validate latency SLOs for short-generation flows, size Dedicated capacity for peak QPS, measure cost per tx with batching+cache, and run end-to-end security review. Agreed to a benchmark run in early Jan using Redwood-hosted test harness against sample traces.
transcript: [00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. Quick roll call, I'm Alex Nguyen from Redwood AE, with Priya Shah our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Marcus: Hey Alex, Marcus here, CTO at ElevatePay. Sam and Daniel on the line too.
[00:11] Samantha: Sam O. Hello.
[00:13] Daniel: Daniel Park, SRE.

[00:18] Priya: Great, our agenda - POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling: QPS, concurrency, token distributions, success criteria, timelines. We'll surface what Redwood needs to size a Dedicated pilot or recommend Hosted config.

[00:35] Marcus: Sounds good. High level: we run fraud scoring, tokenization, and some conversational support workflows. Peak volume is during settlement windows and morning batch spikes. We can share traces but to start high level numbers - baseline 8 QPS steady, spikes to ~45 QPS for 5-10 minutes, average request size varies.

[01:02] Priya: Helpful. Can you break out by endpoint? For instance tokenization calls tend to be tiny inputs, fraud scoring medium prompts, and the conversational support larger generation pieces - that changes batching efficiency and KV cache behavior.

[01:18] Marcus: Sure. Tokenization/auth - ~40% of calls, input ~20 tokens, output ~10 tokens; fraud scoring - 45% calls, input ~120 tokens, output ~40 tokens; conversational fallback / support - 15% calls, input 300-800 tokens (customers pasted statements), output 80-300 tokens. We also run embeddings offline for search, but that's batch and not in the low-latency SLA.

[01:46] Alex: Great, that distribution is exactly what we need. So rough QPS profile: steady 8 QPS, 95th percentile spikes to 40-50 QPS, concurrency during spikes maybe ~12-18 concurrent in-flight requests depending on latency. Is your latency SLO for the online path 300ms or 1s?
[02:05] Samantha: For tokenization and fraud scoring we want p95 under 300ms. For the long conversational generation we can tolerate 1.5s p95 but prefer <1s if possible.

[02:20] Priya: Understood. That implies we need to optimize for low-latency small-requests - those don't batch well, but caching and a smaller model variant can help. For the long generation flows, batching helps and we can use larger quantized models to reduce cost.
[02:40] Daniel: Quick Q: network constraints - we have egress limits inside our VPC and strict firewall rules. We'd prefer a Private deployment but open to Dedicated if rollout speed matters.

[02:52] Alex: Good callout. We'll document both paths. For the POC we usually do a Hosted benchmark first (to prove perf) and then map to Dedicated or Private sizing. That lets us iterate faster while you review the security artifacts.
[03:08] Marcus: Ok. What metrics will you run in the benchmark?

[03:12] Priya: We'll run throughput vs latency curves across the three request classes. Specifically: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail jitter, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per request under different batch profiles and quantization settings. We'll also simulate spike windows using your traces - prefix caching will be toggled on/off to capture impact.
[03:37] Marcus: Prefix caching, interesting. We do a lot of repeated prefixes in fraud scoring - could save a lot if it's cached.

[03:44] Priya: Exactly. For KV/prefix caching we expect big wins on fraud scoring where the user prompts have repeated templates. For tokenization the win is minimal. We'll capture hit/miss rates in the report.
[03:56] Samantha: On models - what do you recommend? We currently evaluate an open 13B for latency and a 70B for quality tests.

[04:05] Priya: For tokenization/fraud scoring a 13B or optimized 7B quantized run often meets p95 200-300ms on A100/RTX-class. For the larger conversational flows, a 70B may be needed for best quality; however we can run a cascaded approach: small model for intent/short replies and fallback to 70B for complex generations. Redwood supports model variants and automatic routing for that pattern.

[04:27] Alex: Also worth noting the economics: batching and quantization reduce per-token cost drastically. We'll include cost sensitivity analysis in the benchmark plan - e.g., 8-bit quantization vs fp16 tradeoffs.
[04:42] Daniel: For sizing Dedicated, what raw numbers do you need?

[04:46] Priya: We'll need: target p95 latency per endpoint, QPS profile over 24 hours (or the traces), percent distribution by request type, median/99th token lengths, and acceptable cost ceiling for the pilot. With that we model GPU counts, steady vs burst capacity (burst nodes), and autoscale policy.
[05:06] Marcus: We can provide traces. For cost ceiling - initial pilot budget is modest, want to validate architecture before committing to a monthly reserved capacity.
[05:15] Priya: No problem. Pilot typically uses a small Dedicated pool or hosted capacity with telemetry turned up. Our benchmark will show expected cost per 1M requests for each config.
[05:26] Samantha: Security - can you send SOC2 and our standard encryption/KMS integration doc? We're particularly concerned about audit logs and key management.
[05:33] Alex: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the KMS/HSM integration guide. For Private/Dedicated we can integrate your KMS and produce audit logs at the route level.
[05:42] Marcus: Good. On timelines - we'd like a short pilot in early Jan, run bench, then decide by end of Jan.

[05:50] Priya: That aligns with our typical flow. Proposed timeline: this week - share traces + initial security docs; week of Jan 4 - Redwood runs benchmark (1-2 days of active testing, 1 hour production-like window for spike tests); week of Jan 11 - discuss results and sizing; by Jan 20 - confirm pilot contract and if Dedicated, start provisioning.
[06:12] Daniel: For the benchmark harness - can you containerize test harness to run inside our VPC? We may prefer that for more realistic network conditions.

[06:19] Priya: Yes, we have a containerized load generator and can either run it from Redwood-hosted infra against Hosted endpoints or provide an image you can run in your VPC pointing at Redwood Dedicated/private endpoints. For the first validation we recommend Redwood-run to speed up iteration.
[06:32] Samantha: On observability - we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. Is that in Console?
[06:37] Alex: Yep, Redwood Console exposes per-route token costs, latency histograms, and trace hooks. We'll show a sample dashboard in the follow-up demo.
[06:45] Marcus: Anything else on traffic modeling? I want to make sure concurrency math accounts for KV cache miss amplification during spikes.

[06:53] Priya: Good point - we'll simulate cache warm/cold states. For concurrency modeling: concurrency = QPS * avg_latency. So with 50 QPS spike and 300ms avg latency you expect ~15 concurrent; if tail jumps to 600ms concurrency doubles. We'll include sensitivity analysis for p95 shifts.
[07:15] Marcus: Nice. Also include network RTT assumptions - our VPC to Redwood region is ~12-18ms RTT.
[07:22] Priya: Noted. We'll add network overhead and client-side processing time into the latency budget.

[07:29] Alex: Recap next steps quickly - Priya will draft the benchmark plan and test scripts; Marcus to share traces; Alex to send security docs and pricing. We'll schedule the benchmark week of Jan 4.
[07:40] Samantha: Confirming - share the sample trace format you prefer?
[07:43] Priya: CSV or gzipped JSONL with fields: timestamp, endpoint, input_tokens, output_tokens, user_id (anonymized), latency_sample if available. We'll send the template.
[07:57] Daniel: One ask - can you capture GPU utilization and per-model memory metrics during the bench so we can compare to our own infra numbers?
[08:03] Priya: Yes, we'll include GPU utilization, memory footprint, batch sizes, and kernel-level metrics where available.
[08:10] Marcus: Great. That should do it. Anything else?
[08:14] Alex: Nothing from us. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites. Talk soon.
[08:19] Marcus: Thanks, bye.
[08:21] Samantha: Bye.
[08:22] Daniel: Bye.
[61:58] [call ended]
